definitions: An electrochemical capacitor that has an unusually high energy density compared to common capacitors, typically 10 to 100 times greater.
A high-capacity electrochemical capacitor with capacitance values much higher than other capacitors, bridging the gap between electrolytic capacitors and rechargeable batteries.
examples: The device uses a super capacitor for quick energy bursts.
Research is ongoing to improve super capacitor technology.
A super capacitor can store a significant amount of energy.
